subject: Film & Cinema
title: Ingmar Bergman: The Soul on Screen
description: A 60-second lesson on Ingmar Bergman: The Soul on Screen.

hook.text: Bergman made films about death, faith, and loneliness. Millions watched anyway.

buildup.text: The Seventh Seal's chess game with Death became the most iconic image in art cinema.

discovery.text: Bergman used close-ups of faces to reveal inner turmoil no dialogue could express.

twist.text: He admitted to deep personal cruelty and depression — his films were partly confessional.

climax.text: Bergman proved cinema could explore the human soul as deeply as any novel or symphony.

punchline.text: He filmed what no one wants to face.

quiz.question: What technique was Bergman famous for?
options: Extreme close-ups of faces to reveal inner emotional states
